name: Mirabegron
route_note: Oral extended-release tablet or granules once daily
owner: Astellas Pharma; generic in the US

discovery.note: A selective beta3-agonist developed for bladder relaxation without antimuscarinic side effects.

tagline: First beta3-agonist for overactive bladder, avoiding anticholinergic effects
summary: Mirabegron is a beta3-adrenergic receptor agonist that relaxes the bladder detrusor during filling. It treats overactive bladder in adults and neurogenic detrusor overactivity in children, with less dry mouth and constipation than antimuscarinics, but can raise blood pressure.
mechanism: Beta3-adrenergic receptors are the predominant beta subtype in detrusor smooth muscle. Mirabegron activates them, increasing cAMP and relaxing the bladder during the storage phase, which increases capacity and reduces urgency episodes.
Because it does not block muscarinic receptors, it lacks typical anticholinergic effects. It is a moderate CYP2D6 inhibitor, raising levels of drugs such as metoprolol and desipramine.
uses: Overactive bladder with urge incontinence, urgency and frequency (alone or with solifenacin)
Neurogenic detrusor overactivity in children aged 3 years and older

history.title: Japanese approval
history.detail: Mirabegron (Betanis) is first approved in Japan.

history.title: US and EU approval
history.detail: FDA approves Myrbetriq in June; the European Commission approves Betmiga in December.

history.title: Combination therapy
history.detail: FDA approves use with solifenacin based on the SYNERGY trials.

history.title: Paediatric use
history.detail: FDA approves mirabegron for neurogenic detrusor overactivity in children.

history.title: US generics
history.detail: Generic extended-release mirabegron launches in the US.

pk.metabolism: Multiple pathways: glucuronidation, amide hydrolysis, CYP3A4 and CYP2D6 oxidation, butyrylcholinesterase

serious: Urinary retention (with bladder outlet obstruction or antimuscarinics)

facts: Mirabegron was the first drug of a new class for overactive bladder in about 30 years.
Vibegron, a second beta3-agonist, was approved in the US in 2020.
